note: 56 findings from a code+screenshot audit of the sample-data site (not user testing). status contested = verifiers disagreed on severity; unverified = low severity, not re-checked.

findings.title: Works and prices are 6-8 screens down, and the desktop header has no link to them
findings.task: Browse available works, search by artist or title, filter by price
findings.evidence: index.html:709 desktop header = City, About, EN/LO, Join only. circles.css:19 shows .menu-btn only at max-width:860px and circles.css:225-227 shows #bnav only below 768px, so at 1280px #featured, #how and #map are reachable only by scrolling or via the footer menu, which is inside a closed <details> (index.html:889; th-desk-index-full.jpg bottom shows the collapsed bar 'เมนู โซเชียล และจดหมายข่าว'). Studio, profile and buy headers are the same (City, About, Join; en-desk-studio-napha.jpg). Playwright measurement: first priced work card at y=5250 of 9726 at 1280x800 (6.6 screens) and y=6247 of 9957 at 375x740 (8.4 screens). In between: hero, city strip, Manifesto (682-887px), 'The loop' (739-813px), How it works (814px desktop, 1630px on phone). The search box (index.html:821) sits inside that wall. Phones do have an 'Art' tab (circles.js:544); desktop has nothing equivalent.
findings.why: Search, the price chips and the 30-work inventory are the main findability tools, and desktop buyers cannot see or reach them from the header on any page. They must scroll through three brand-story sections or open a collapsed footer. A buyer who wants to compare prices only sees abstract buildings with no price, so some leave before the wall. The brand story sits between the visitor and the product.
findings.fix: 1) Add 'ผลงาน / Works' (-> #featured) and 'ศิลปิน / Artists' (-> #map) to the desktop header on every page, using the exact words of the phone bottom bar; keep Join as the pink button. 2) Move the works wall, or at least a 6-card 'available now' row with prices, directly under the city strip, and push Manifesto / The loop below it (or merge them into one short band). 3) Render the footer menu open at >=861px (drop the <details> there). Keep all styles: 3px borders, hard shadows, same tokens.

verification.note:
I re-read the cited code. I did not run Playwright, so I did not re-measure the pixel offsets (y=5250 and y=6247) and am taking them from the finding.

Confirmed in the current code:
- The desktop header is incomplete. index.html:709 shows only #city, #manifesto, the EN language button and Join. The hamburger (.menu-btn) is also in that row.
- The hamburger is hidden on desktop. circles.css:9 sets it to display:none, and it appears only inside @media(max-width:860px) (circles.css:19). At 1280px it is not shown.
- The phone bottom bar is phone-only. circles.css:225-226 sets .bnav to display:none, then shows it only at max-width:767.98px. So desktop has no route to Works, Artists or Map from the header.
- Section order matches the finding. In index.html the sections run city (730), manifesto (753), cycle "The loop" (764), how (782), featured (812), spotlight (833). The works wall (#featured) comes after the three brand-story sections.
- The footer menu is collapsed. index.html:889 is a closed <details class="fold fold-foot">.
- The mnav list at line 710 does contain #featured and #map, but it is reachable only through the hamburger, which is hidden above 860px.

Two softening points:
1. The city strip sits directly under the hero, so a buyer can reach artist studios (and their priced works) early. The hero CTA (line 721) goes to #city. This makes the problem one of discoverability, not a dead end.
2. #map (line 748) is a hidden alternate view of the city strip (the "ดูแบบแผนที่" toggle), not a separate section. A header link to #map would need to switch views, or the link should point to #city instead.

The core claim holds: on desktop, the works wall with prices and search has no header link on the home page and is far down the scroll. I rate it medium rather than high because the studio entry points are visible early and phones have an Art tab.

I checked the evidence and it holds. At index.html:709 the desktop `.links` holds only City, About, the language toggle and Join. `.menu-btn` appears only at max-width:860px (circles.css:19). The `#mnav` links to #how, #featured and #map are therefore unreachable from the header at 1280px. The finding is real, and Works and Artists belong in the desktop header. I weaken it for three reasons. (1) Severity: the page is a one-page scroll, and a buyer can still reach the wall by scrolling or by the hero and city strip, so this is a high-friction path, not a blocked one. Adding the links is a one-line change, which makes it a quick win rather than a structural defect. Medium fits better. (2) Fix step 2 is too heavy and risks the brand. Moving the works wall above the Manifesto and The loop changes the narrative order the identity relies on: story first, then shop. That makes the home page a store front and rewrites the layout of a static page for a beginner developer, which is not an M-sized job. It also isn't needed once the header and hero point to #featured. (3) Fix step 3 (drop the `<details>` at >=861px) only needs CSS, but it is a minor extra. Once the header links exist, the footer menu is redundant for this task. Step 1 is correct and cheap, and it should be the whole core fix.

findings.title: First viewport shows no artwork or price, and the main action is below the fold or under the phone bar
findings.task: Understand in 5 seconds what is sold and start browsing
findings.evidence: Playwright, hero CTA 'เข้าชมเมือง →' (index.html:721): top=814 at 1280x800 and 1366x768, so it is below the fold; at 1440x900 it only just fits. The lead paragraph is cut at y=779 (ux-ia/first-th-1366x768.png). At 375x667 the CTA is at 585-647 (TH) or 618-679 (EN) while #bnav occupies 603-667, so it is partly or fully covered (ux-ia/first-en-375x667.png). The first-visit loader (site.js:474-487) holds the screen for about 3 s; the lead and CTA are not visible at 3000 ms and appear at about 4500 ms (first-visit-3000.png, first-visit-4500.png). th-desk-index.jpg and th-mob-index.jpg show no artwork or price, only the ransom 'CIRCLES', three poetic lines and a tartan arch. 'ซื้อตรงจากคนทำ' is in the small, low-contrast lead. Where the CTA lands: at 1280x800 scrollY=878 shows the header, Buildings/Map toggle and 11 chips, and the first building only starts about 170px from the bottom (after-cta2-1280.png). At 375 the first building starts at y=697, under the bar (after-cta-375.png).
findings.why: The 5-second test: a buyer gets 'city of artists, no middleman' but not what kind of objects, what prices, or what to press. On common laptop sizes and short phones the action is not on screen, and on tap it lands on a control panel instead of the city. Phone users have the City tab as a fallback, so this is not total failure. But for a shared-link or ad visitor the page reads as a brand poster, and leaving costs nothing.
findings.fix: Give the hero one concrete sentence of what is for sale, in plain type under the headline: for example 'Original paintings, photos, ceramics and textiles. Message the artist, pay them directly.' Put 3 real work cards with prices (reuse .card/.plate) in the hero or immediately below it. Set the hero to min-height: calc(100svh - nav - var(--bn-h)) and keep the CTA inside it. Add scroll-margin-top and collapse the City heading and pager on phones so the strip, not the controls, fills the screen after the CTA. Skip the loader once the hero text is ready or after about 600 ms.

verification.note:
I could not run Playwright or a browser here (no playwright module), so I did not re-measure pixel positions. I checked the code and the auditor's screenshots instead.

Code:
- index.html:98 sets .hero to min-height:min(94vh,1000px) with padding-top 4rem. The hero copy has a kicker, a ransom-letter h1, three headline blocks, the lead and then the CTA (index.html:710-721). It also sits under a marquee and a nav, so the CTA falling below 768px is plausible.
- circles.css:227-229 fixes #bnav at the bottom of the screen, 64px tall, on phones.
- The hero contains no work card, artwork image or price, only the tartan arch with the logo (index.html:713-727).
- site.js:474-487 shows the loader on first visit. The count runs 1700ms, then the loader fades and boot() removes the pre class 520ms later. The loader is skipped when the visitor has already seen it (sessionStorage) or has reduced motion on.

Screenshots (first-th-1366x768.png, first-en-375x667.png):
- At 1366x768 the lead paragraph is cut off at the bottom of the screen and the CTA is not visible. No artwork or price is shown.
- At 375x667 EN the lead ends right above the bottom bar and the CTA is not visible. It is hidden under #bnav, as claimed.

Corrections:
- Phones have the City tab in #bnav as a fallback, and the loader only shows on a visitor's first view in a session.
- The loader timing (about 3s, 4.5s) and the post-CTA landing positions were not re-measured, though the code makes a delay of that order plausible. The loader code alone gives about 2.2s.
- I would rate this medium rather than high, because users can still scroll or use the bottom bar.

The problem is real, and the code supports the evidence. The hero uses min-height min(94vh,1000px) and the CTA is the last item after a 7-step rise animation. The loader runs a 1.7s count plus a 520ms boot delay, so the lead and CTA appear about 2.2s or more after load. This only happens on a first visit. It is skipped when sessionStorage 'circles-seen' is set or when reduced motion is on. The loader's 6s safety net also exists.

I would still lower severity from high to medium. Desktop has a scroll cue and the CTA is one scroll away. Phone has the City tab in #bnav. Nothing is blocked. The loss is that the buyer gets an unclear message and a slower start. The CTA being covered by the bar on a 667px-tall phone is a real but narrow bug.

The proposed fix bundles five changes, and that is too much for a beginner developer. Three real work cards inside the hero add data and layout work and compete with the poster identity. They would also duplicate the works wall that sits right below. The loader point is the cheapest and clearest win. The hero min-height point is worth keeping. The sentence about what is sold is a good idea, but it should replace the weak lead text, not be added on top of it.

findings.title: The works wall shows 8 of 30 works and ends without a 'see all' step
findings.task: See every available work
findings.evidence: site.js:281 FEAT is a fixed list of 8 picks; site.js:314 uses it unless a filter is on; site.js:341 prints 'แสดง 8 ชิ้น' (Showing 8 works) without the total until a filter is on. The only way to the other 22 works is the 'ทั้งหมด 30' chip inside the filter panel (index.html:823). th-desk-index-full.jpg (works wall) ends with the 8th card and goes straight into the Spotlight section. The same destination is called 'Art/ผลงาน' (circles.js:544, bottom bar), 'Featured/ผลงานเด่น' (hamburger) and 'This week's picks' (heading). Tapping the 'Art' tab at 375x740 leaves the filter panel on screen and the first card at top=733, behind the bar at 676 (ux-ia/bn-art.png).
findings.why: A buyer who tapped 'Art' expects the art, sees a form-like panel, then 8 cards and no continuation. 73% of the inventory is invisible by default, and the one control that reveals it is a status chip, not something people would call 'see everything'.
findings.fix: After the last card add a full-width brutalist button 'ดูผลงานทั้งหมด 30 ชิ้น →' that runs the same code as the 'ทั้งหมด' chip. Always show 'แสดง 8 จาก 30 ชิ้น'. On phones collapse the panel to one search line plus a 'Filter (n)' button so the first card shows under the heading, and give #featured a scroll-margin so the 'Art' tab lands on the first row.

verification.note:
I re-read the code and the claim holds. site.js:281 FEAT has exactly 8 picks. site.js:314 uses FEAT unless wholeCity() is true, which means F.all is set or a filter or query is active. site.js:341 prints feat_count 'แสดง {n} ชิ้น' / 'Showing {n} works' with no total when no filter is on. The 'of total' form (sf_count) only appears once a filter is on. index.html:812-831 has nothing between #masonry and the closing </section>, so there is no 'see all' button after the 8th card. The next element is the tape-wrap, then the Spotlight section. The only control that reveals the rest is the 'ทั้งหมด' chip (#all-btn, index.html:823), which sits inside the filter panel above the grid. bn_art is 'ผลงาน' / 'Art' in circles.js:45 and :116. The heading is 'ผลงานเด่นสัปดาห์นี้' (feat_h). I did not run the page, so I did not re-check the 375px tab-landing offset (top=733 behind the bar at 676) or the 30-works total. I took both from the auditor's evidence.

Two things weaken it. The chip is not hidden. The filter panel is always visible directly above the grid, and the chip carries a live count, so a motivated visitor can find it. Search and the price chips also widen the list to the whole city. The real gap is that nothing at the end of the wall points on to the rest. Medium is fair, and low-medium is arguable.

Evidence checks out. FEAT is a fixed list of 8 (site.js:281). worksList() uses it unless wholeCity() is true. The heading uses feat_count with no total until a filter is on (renderFeatured). So 22 of 30 works sit behind a status chip inside the filter panel. This is a real findability problem and medium is about right, because the filter chip is the only route and 'Art' is a primary nav label. The 'see all' button is the right core fix: it is small, reuses the existing F.all path, and fits the brand. The proposed fix bundles three separate changes, and two of them are weaker. (1) Collapsing the panel into 'search + Filter (n)' on phones is a new component with new states, strings, focus handling and a rebuild. That is too much for a beginner developer. The first-card-hidden problem comes from scroll position, not from the panel's existence. (2) 'Always show 8 of 30' is cheap and good, but it needs a new string key in both STR.th and STR.en, and the existing sf_count already takes n and t. (3) The scroll-margin on #featured is the cheapest fix for the Art tab landing and does most of the job. Also keep the label consistent: use one word ('ผลงาน' / 'Art') across the bottom bar, hamburger and heading, which costs nothing.

findings.title: One destination, several names; three navigation systems overlap; place words drift
findings.task: Predict where a link goes and find the way back to something seen earlier
findings.evidence: index.html:709-710 and circles.js strings. Header 'About/เกี่ยวกับ' goes to #manifesto, a slogan wall, not an about page. Works are 'Art' (bottom bar), 'Featured' (hamburger and footer) and 'This week's picks' (heading). The map is 'Artists' (bottom bar), 'City map' (hamburger) and 'Map' (toggle). The artist action is 'Join' (index.html:709, hard-coded English, no data-t), 'Get a building' (foot_join), 'Request to join →' (foot_btn), 'Join — get a building →' (join_btn) and 'See how it works →' (jb_btn, index.html:864). That last one collides with the buyer section #how on the same page. Join opens a dialog from the header and the footer button but goes to join.html from the join band and the hamburger. Place words: building, studio, museum, hall, district (pf_walk 'Walk into the museum', spot_cta 'Enter Napha's building', buy back link 'Back to Napha's museum', fnote 'district'). On a 375px page the language switch appears twice (header button plus bottom bar), and 3 of the 6 hamburger items repeat the bottom bar (ux-ia/menu-375-index.png).
findings.why: Visitors build a map from labels. With a metaphor-heavy site (city, building, museum, district) and different words for the same target, people cannot tell whether 'Artists', 'City map' and 'City' are three places or one. 'See how it works' on the artist band sounds like the buyer explainer. The same words in three nav bars make it unclear which one to trust.
findings.fix: Pick one vocabulary and use it in the header, hamburger, bottom bar and footer: City · Works · Artists · How it works · For artists. Rename 'About' to 'How it works' (or add a real About page), rename 'Featured / This week's picks' to 'Works', and make 'Artists' the same target everywhere. Use one place word ('building' or 'studio') and drop 'museum'. Rename the join band button to 'For artists: details →'. Make the pink header button go to join.html (see IA-5). On phones remove the hamburger items that the bottom bar already carries.

verification.note: Checked index.html and circles.js on current code. TRUE: header 'About' (nav_about) links to #manifesto (index.html:709). Header Join is hard-coded English with no data-t, and it calls openJoin(), a dialog. The footer button (index.html:888) also calls openJoin(), while the join band (index.html:864, jb_btn) and the hamburger foot_join go to join.html. Label drift is real. Works are bn_art 'Art' / foot_feat 'Featured' / feat_h "This week's picks". The map is bn_artists 'Artists' / foot_map 'City map' / nav_map 'Map', and the bottom bar's 'Artists' goes to #map (circles.js:544). The artist action has the labels foot_join, foot_btn, join_btn and jb_btn. 'See how it works →' (EN jb_btn) is on the artist band, and #how at line 782 is the buyer explainer, so the collision is real. Place words differ: pf_walk 'museum', spot_cta 'building', fnote 'district'. The hamburger has 6 items (city, manifesto, how, featured, map, join); 3 (city, featured, map) duplicate the 3 bottom-bar targets. The language switch is in both the header (#lang) and the bottom bar (bn_lang). Not checked: the screenshot, the 375px render, and the buy back link text. Impact is modest: this is a label-consistency issue and nothing is broken. In the Thai UI the Thai strings are mostly consistent ('ผลงาน' / 'ผลงานเด่น', 'แผนที่เมือง'), so the drift hits English most. 'Medium' overstates it; low to medium.

The problem is real. Checked index.html lines 709, 710, 864 and 891. Header "เกี่ยวกับ" (data-t nav_about) goes to #manifesto. The header "Join" is hard-coded English and has no data-t. The hamburger and footer use different labels for the same targets (Manifesto, ผลงานเด่น, แผนที่เมือง, ขอมีตึก). The join band button (jb_btn) reads "ดูรายละเอียด" and goes to join.html, while the header opens a dialog. Medium severity is right: it hurts wayfinding and trust but blocks no purchase. Two parts of the fix need changing. (1) "Rename About to How it works" is wrong, because #manifesto and #how are two different sections on the same page. Renaming one link to the other's name would create a new collision. The link should say what it opens: "Manifesto" or "Why circles". "How it works" should point only to #how. (2) The proposed vocabulary (City · Works · Artists · How it works · For artists) is too big a change for one beginner developer. It also hides the artist-versus-buyer split, which the join band already handles. The "drop museum" idea fights the brand metaphor (the museum is the picture hall, a legitimate place), so it should be limited to one word per object type, not a site-wide purge. Strings live in STR.th and STR.en in circles.js, so a label sweep is cheap. Pushing the pink header button to join.html belongs to IA-5, so IA-4 should not depend on it. Removing hamburger items on phones adds responsive logic and risks a dead-end menu. The simpler cure for the duplicate navigation is to keep the items but use identical wording, or to hide only the two true duplicates (language and City) under 768px with CSS.

findings.title: Artist path: the pitch sits at 85% scroll, the Join button skips it, and the promise contradicts itself
findings.task: Decide to apply and know what happens after sending
findings.evidence: The only artist cue in the first viewport is the pink 'Join' (index.html:709), which opens the application dialog (circles.js:467-485) without any pitch. The pitch band #join is at y=8507 of 9957 on a phone and y=8251 of 9726 on desktop (85%). join.html's only action (join.html:101) is at y=1005 on desktop (viewport 800) and y=1698 of 2029 on a 375px phone, below three stacked perk cards. Copy says 'No jury' and 'ไม่มีคนคัดงาน / nobody judges the work' (join.html sticker, p3_h, jb_p), but the dialog is titled 'Request a building' and says 'เราดูที่งาน / We look at the work' (jd_title, jd_intro, foot_p). Nowhere is there what to prepare, what happens next, or that there is no checkout (buyers message the artist and the artist arranges payment). The hero never mentions artists. A buyer can also read 'Join' as account sign-up.
findings.why: An artist deciding whether to hand over a link and email needs: is this reviewed or automatic, what do I get, what do I do after, how do I get paid. The page answers none of the last three and sends mixed signals on the first. The buyer-facing header button is also ambiguous.
findings.fix: Add a quiet text link under the hero CTA: 'For artists: get a building →' (join.html). Change the pink header button label to 'For artists / สำหรับศิลปิน' (or keep 'ขอมีตึก') and point it to join.html. On join.html move the button into the hero and add a 3-step 'what happens next' (send link, we reply by email, you get your building), 'what to prepare' and 'how buyers reach you and pay'. Use one honest word for the screening (open, or reviewed). Fill in reply time and requirements only once the owner has real values; leave out what is unknown, as SHIPPING and RATES already do.

verification.note: I read the code and did not run the page, so the scroll offsets (85%, y=8507, y=1698) are unchecked. Confirmed in code: (1) The pink header "Join" button at index.html:709 calls openJoin(), which opens the dialog directly. The only other join link is in the mobile menu (index.html:711, "ขอมีตึก" to join.html). (2) The copy does mix signals. p3_h is "ไม่มีใครคัดงาน / No one judges the work" (circles.js:77, 148) and jb_p says "no jury" (circles.js:78, 149). The dialog title is "Request a building" with the intro "We look at the work" (jd_title and jd_intro, circles.js:84, 154). foot_p says the same (circles.js:79, 150). "Request" and "we look at the work" do imply review, so the contradiction is mild but real. (3) join.html:101 holds the single button after three perk cards, as claimed. Overstated: "nowhere is what happens next" is not true. jn_cta (join.html:101, circles.js:78 and 149) says "tell us what you make, add a link, and we will get back to you by email". That covers the send-link and reply-by-email steps. What is missing is what to prepare, reply time, and how buyers pay, and I did not check the buy flow for that. Also, "the hero never mentions artists" and "a buyer may read Join as sign-up" are judgment calls I could not test. Net: the finding is a real but minor copy and IA problem, not a medium-severity comprehension blocker.

Evidence checks out. index.html:709 has the pink Join button calling openJoin() (dialog, no pitch). The mobile menu already links to join.html as 'ขอมีตึก' (foot_join). join.html's only CTA sits after the 3 perk cards. The copy conflict is real: perk 3 says 'ไม่ต้องมีใครคัดงาน' and the dialog/foot_p say 'เราดูที่งาน / we look at the work'. The 'no checkout' point is a real comprehension gap for artists. Severity medium is fair: it affects only the artist path and does not block buyers. The fix is mostly right but bundles too much. (a) Rerouting the header button to join.html adds a page hop for artists who are already convinced, and the dialog is a working shortcut. Relabelling it is the cheap win ('ขอมีตึก' / 'Get a building' removes the account-signup reading). Keep the dialog, or open join.html only for first-time visitors. (b) Adding a hero text link is fine but optional, since #join band and footer already exist. (c) The 3-step 'what happens next' block and the 'how buyers reach you' line are the high-value part. They must contain only true facts, because the CLAUDE.md rule is never to invent values. (d) Moving the button into the hero on join.html is good and cheap. (e) The most valuable and cheapest change is fixing the contradictory copy to one honest word, since it is a plain string edit in circles.js (both th and en).

findings.title: No real contact or help path on the home page, and visible placeholders erode trust
findings.task: Decide the site is real and get help before messaging a stranger to pay
findings.evidence: The home page has no contact, FAQ or 'who runs this'. Outside the closed footer fold the footer shows only the copyright line plus Privacy and Terms (index.html:904). The only contact is mailto:hello@circles.example, shown on buy pages ('ปลอดภัยไหม?', links.txt) and on the legal pages, and it uses a reserved .example domain. privacy.html shows a yellow 'This is a template... [add legal entity and address here]' banner on the live look (en-mob-privacy.jpg), and it is the target of every form's consent line (circles.js:477, 496). Placeholder UI shown as live: three footer social links are href='#' with a toast 'open when the site goes live' (index.html:893-895); a full home section 'Support' whose only button is disabled 'เร็วๆ นี้' (index.html:867-872); the same disabled 'Support Napha' box on every profile (profile.js:38-39, th-desk-profile-napha-full.jpg).
findings.why: Buying is 'email the artist, then pay them directly', which is a high-trust leap. The visitor who wants to ask 'who runs this, how do I pay safely, what if it never arrives' finds no help on the home page. Disabled buttons and dead social links tell them the product is unfinished. The README already lists these as go-live tasks, but nothing keeps them off the live look.
findings.fix: On the live look hide the Support section, the social list and the per-artist support box until a real value exists (same approach as the [__] rule: check CONFIG.donate and real social URLs). Put the operator name and a real contact line in the footer outside the fold. Add a short FAQ band (How do I pay? Shipping? Original or print? Who runs this?) in place of 'The loop', and link it from the buy page's 'Is it safe?' card. Finish privacy.html and terms.html and remove the template notice before launch.

verification.note: Checked current code. Home footer (index.html:~904) shows only the copyright line (which itself says "prototype, artists and works are samples") plus Privacy and Terms. The home page has no contact, FAQ or operator info. The only contact is CONFIG.contact = hello@circles.example (circles.js:9), rendered on the buy page (buy.js:66) and in privacy.html:107. privacy.html:103 has an unconditional yellow `.draft` banner ("This is a template...") and a "[add legal entity and address here]" placeholder, with no isDraft gating. Social links at index.html:893-895 are href="#" with a toast, inside the closed details fold. The Support section (index.html:867-872) has a disabled "เร็วๆ นี้" button. site.js:432-438 hides only the .sup-w breakdown box, not the section or button. The per-profile disabled support button is at profile.js:39. Corrections: the social links are inside the closed footer fold, so they are less visible than implied. The footer copyright already says "prototype", so some honesty signal exists. The page is a labelled prototype, so severity could be low. The claim is real, but the reproduction is by code reading only, and I ran no browser.

Evidence checked in index.html: disabled 'เร็วๆ นี้' donate button (872) and three href='#' social links with a 'soon' toast (893-895) are real. The problem is real: dead links and disabled buttons read as unfinished, and a buyer who has to pay a stranger needs a contact line. findings.title: On phones the send result lands off-screen, so a failed send looks like a success

findings.evidence: buy.js:114-123 swaps .by-box innerHTML with no scrollIntoView or focus. Measured on buy-napha-1.html?live (th, touch): at 375x740 the document shrinks from 3334 to 2893px and .by-done ends at top -76 / bottom 70 (under the 72px nav). At 375x667 it ends at top -149 / bottom -3. Desktop 1280 is fine (top 437, in view). Screenshots ux-buy/B2-success.png and ux-buy/C1-fail.png show only the card 'ส่งแล้วจะเห็นข้อความ: “ส่งถึงนภาแล้ว คำตอบจะส่งไปที่อีเมลของคุณ”' plus the footer, for success and for a Formspree 422 alike. While sending, show 'กำลังส่ง…' / 'Sending…' on the button with a stepped hazard-stripe fill (steps(1,end), matching the site's cut-and-paste motion) and aria-busy. findings.title: When sending fails or the captcha does not load, the buyer is stuck and loses what they typed

The only action is 'ส่งอีกข้อความ' (by_again, buy.js:119), which rebuilds the default form. Verified after retry: name '', email '', message back to the prefill. The buy page also drops the copy/mailto fallback (buy.js:117 `ok || fail ? '' : …`), while the dialog shows To: + the message + Copy (circles.js:434-436). (b) If challenges.cloudflare.com is blocked or slow, the form can never be sent. circles.js:451 shows only toast 'รอให้การตรวจสอบเสร็จก่อนส่ง' for 2.6s, .cf-holder stays empty (verified ux-buy D1) and nothing else is offered. 1. Failure (a) is the biggest problem, and it is a bug rather than a design gap. The simplest correct fix is to stop replacing the form on failure. Keep the form, re-enable the button (wireForm already does this in `finally`), and show the error in a role=alert line above the button.
2. The mailto link and Copy button are the real safety net. They should serve all three cases (send failed, captcha blocked, nothing sent). Build them once as a small helper that is also used for the 'done_mail' mode.
3. Do not add a 4s Turnstile timer. Make the fallback visible from the start under the submit button as a quiet line, 'ส่งไม่ได้? ส่งอีเมลหาศิลปินเอง' (Can't send? findings.evidence: site.js:476-487: DUR=1700 count-up that must finish before `go()`, then loader slide transition 1.15s (index.html:282) and boot at +520ms, 6s safety timeout; loader is aria-hidden and has no skip/tap-to-skip. circles.js:650-680 + circles.css:78-86: `html.pgc-in::after` black full-screen overlay (safety 1.5s) and a .pgc curtain 0.4s that plays between pages. The loader count-up is DUR=1700ms and go() only runs after Promise.all([fontsReady, counted]). go() then adds .done, the slide-out transition at index.html:282 (not read, assumed to be the 1.15s the finding cites). boot() runs 520ms later and there is a 6s safety timeout. The #loader element is aria-hidden="true" with no click or key handler to skip it. The seen flag is in sessionStorage, so it is skipped only within one tab session or under reduced motion. The page curtain intercepts every plain click on a same-origin .html link. That includes buy and profile pages, since the only exclusions are same-page links, modified clicks and target/download links. It waits 430ms before navigating, and html.pgc-in::after is a black overlay with a 1.5s safety timer. Arrival then adds a 260ms hold plus a 450ms lift. Overstated parts: the loader is shown once per tab session, not on every visit. The effective curtain cost is about 0.4s out plus about 0.7s in per navigation, not the loader's ~3s. A real first-time visitor, or one opening the site in a new tab, still waits about 1.7s plus the slide-out before the city is visible. Buyers pay about 1s per page hop.

Evidence checks out. site.js: DUR=1700 count must resolve (Promise.all with fonts) before go(); then boot at +520ms; sessionStorage seen flag; no skip. circles.js pageCurtain: every same-origin .html click delays navigation 430ms, then the arriving page holds the curtain about 260ms plus 450ms lift. Real cost, mostly on the home first visit (about 2.2-2.7s before the city shows) and on every buy-path hop. Severity medium is fair, since the loader is brand identity and is session-only. But the fix is over-scoped. Replacing sessionStorage with a 24h localStorage timestamp adds a storage and expiry decision for little gain. Limiting the curtain by page type needs a URL-pattern whitelist, which is more code and a new rule to maintain. Cutting to 0.9s while keeping the fake count is a half-measure.

findings.title: Skip-to-content link exists only on join.html
findings.task: Keyboard/screen-reader users bypassing the nav and the 10-building city strip
findings.evidence: `<a class="skip" href="#main">` appears only in join.html:78 (CSS join.html:29). Measured: skip link present on join, absent on index, buy, profile, studio. Home has a large tab-stop sequence (nav, 10 building links, pager, chips) before the works wall. profile.html renders its top-level heading as `<h2 class="pf-name">` (profile.js:45) and measured 0 h1 on profile-napha.
findings.why: Keyboard users must tab through the nav and the 10-building strip on every page load; missing h1 on profile pages weakens heading navigation for screen readers.
findings.fix: Move the .skip rule into circles.css and inject the link in circles.js wireNav() on every page (target #main, which exists in buy/profile); make the profile name an h1 (keep the .pf-sr text).

verification.note: I grepped the templates and shared scripts statically. I did not run the page or count tab stops in a browser, so the "large tab-stop sequence" claim is unmeasured. (1) The only `class="skip"` link is at join.html:78. Index, buy, profile, cutaway, privacy, terms and 404 have none. circles.js has no skip-link injection. Its only skip reference is the `skip_main` string (circles.js:78 and 149), which only join.html uses. (2) `id="main"` exists on `<main>` in buy.html:110, profile.html:110 and cutaway.html:410, so the proposed target works there. I did not find `id="main"` in index.html. The grep pattern would have matched it, so the home page needs a target added. (3) profile.js:45 renders the artist name as `<h2 class="pf-name">`. profile.html has an `<h1>` only inside the `<noscript>` and not-found fallbacks, and profile.js has no `<h1>`. A loaded profile page therefore has no h1, as claimed. Index (index.html:716), cutaway (516) and buy (buy.js:51) each have an h1. Both claims hold, though they are low-to-medium impact: the skip link is missing on every page except join, and profile pages lack an h1.

Verified. The skip link exists only in join.html:78. Buy, profile and cutaway have <main id="main">, but index.html has no <main> and no #main (it only has section#city at line 730). So injecting a link with target #main on every page would break on the home page, which is the page that needs it most. Severity medium is fair. WCAG 2.4.1 (bypass blocks) is level A, but a landmark or heading can also satisfy it, so it is not critical. The h1 part is accurate: profile.js:45 uses h2.pf-name with no h1 on the page. CSS for .pf-name is class-only (profile.css:42), so changing the tag to h1 is safe, with no visual change. The profile's aria-labelledby=pf-name still works. Injecting from circles.js is reasonable and fits the rule 'use shared helpers'. The fix as written is incomplete, because index lacks #main. It also has a timing risk: the profile page renders main.innerHTML from JS, so #main must exist in the static HTML (it does in buy/profile/cutaway), and the link must be the first focusable element in body, so it must be prepended, not appended.

findings.title: Muted greys fall under AA on the bone surface, and pink/gold are unusable as text on light surfaces
findings.task: Read secondary notes and avoid future contrast regressions
findings.evidence: #6E685C is 4.90:1 on paper but 4.35:1 on bone (fails 4.5 for small text); used for 12.8px Special Elite notes at index.html:218 (.wl, on paper, passes), index.html:607 (.sup-note, on paper, passes), circles.css:40 (.cdlg .note). Other combinations that fail: pink on paper 3.10, pink on bone 2.75, gold on paper 1.65, tartan-red on black 2.52, black on tartan-red 2.52, gold on tartan-red 4.13, concrete #8F8C85 on paper 2.97 / on bone 2.64. Today none of the failing pairs is used for body text, but the greys sit only 0.1-0.4 above the limit and three different hexes (#6E685C, #4a4642, #5E584D, #4A453D) exist outside the 7-token palette.
findings.why: Any note moved onto the bone background, or any pink/gold label placed on paper, would silently fail; four extra grey hexes also break the 'never add a new hex' rule and make a designer's Figma styles inconsistent.
findings.fix: Add one token `--ink-2:#4A453D` (8.41 on paper, ~7.4 on bone) to replace #6E685C/#4a4642/#5E584D; document that pink and gold are text colours on black only, and that --concrete is decorative or large-text only.

findings.title: Hover-dependent affordances: quick-view details, tag walk-link and card plate
findings.task: Find the 'walk in the studio' and quick view on a laptop trackpad
findings.evidence: Tag .wl (walk link) opacity 0 until :hover/:focus-visible on desktop (index.html:217-219; always shown only under hover:none index.html:388); gallery hint `.pf-hv` and plate text depend on hover (profile.js:53 `pf_hover`). missing_areas.why: Every string exists in two languages and Lao is mostly missing. Nobody checked tone consistency, translation parity, Thai type fit (line height, wrapping) or terminology drift beyond navigation names. Thai is the primary audience.

missing_areas.why: The site is heavy on animation (HD2D scene, loader, curtain, Lenis smooth scroll) and relies on a lite mode. Only the loader delay was noted. Nobody measured load, interaction latency or image weight on the mid-range Android phones most Thai visitors use.

missing_areas.topic: Artist onboarding after acceptance and artist-side management
missing_areas.why: Join stops at 'we will email you'. Nobody examined how an artist adds works, sets price or marks a work sold, since artists.js is edited by the owner. This decides whether the supply side can scale.
After the message is sent, nobody examined the buyer's journey: reply expectations, payment confirmation, shipping tracking, disputes. This links directly to the trust and protection findings.

missing_areas.why: Only some items were checked. Dialogs, the lightbox, the city strip and the map need keyboard and screen-reader paths.

missing_areas.topic: Analytics and success measurement, plus SEO and share-link entry
missing_areas.why: Nobody defined funnel metrics (wall view to quick view to buy page to sent message) or checked how visitors from search and social share cards land on deep pages, which are the real entry points.

themes.theme: The buying path is buried and fragmented: the wall is far down, the nav does not lead to it, and one work appears in several surfaces with different content
Decision-critical information (price, artist, status, Buy button) is hidden, delayed or placed below the first screen, especially on phones
Trust and honesty gap: labels and promises do not match what the product does, and the live site shows placeholders, a fake contact and no protection for large payments
Dead ends and unclear feedback in the contact flow, plus sold or reserved works with no next step
Stacked fixed layers, small tap targets and small text make phones cramped and hard to use
State, naming and system consistency are weak: filters and sort are untrusted, language handling diverges and navigation names drift

top_priorities.reason: A failed send looks like a success on phones because the result lands off-screen, so a buyer can believe the artist was contacted when nothing was sent. This is the core conversion step.
A failed send or an unloaded captcha is a dead end that wipes what the buyer typed, so a motivated buyer is lost permanently.
The sticky buy bar covers the message field on the buy page while the buyer types, which blocks the main task on phones.
Works and prices sit 6-8 screens down and the desktop header has no link to them, so most visitors never reach what is for sale (DISCOVERY-1 is the same problem seen from the discovery side).
The first viewport shows no artwork or price and the primary CTA is below the fold or under the phone bar, so the 5-second pitch fails.
Price, title and artist are hidden until hover on the desktop wall (the same issue as DISCOVERY-3), so scanning and comparing is impossible. This is a cheap fix with large effect.
There is no named operator and the contact address is fake, so buyers cannot trust the site enough to send a four-figure payment.
There is no baht price, shipping, payment method, returns or reply time, so a buyer cannot decide before messaging.
On phones the Prev/Next buttons are separate from the label that holds price, status and Buy, so the content changes off screen while walking the hall.
Sort by price reorders only 8 picks and reads as scrambled, which breaks trust in the main way to find cheaper works.

conflicts: IA-1 and DISCOVERY-1 propose making the works wall reachable from the header and hero, while IA-2 asks for artwork and price in the first viewport. Doing both puts two competing primary actions above the fold. Pick one lead action (browse works) and make the artist 'Join' path secondary (IA-5, ARTISTSIDE-8).

IA-5 wants the artist pitch moved up or shown before the Join form, while IA-2 and IA-1 want the buyer's works moved up. Both claim the same top-of-page space. Resolve it by audience: buyers first on the home page, artists via a dedicated pitch page before the form.

ARTISTSIDE-5 and IA-5 say the 'no jury' promise contradicts the right to refuse. The fix is to soften or reword the promise, but that weakens the artist pitch, which ARTISTSIDE-6 says is already vague about cost. Rewrite the claims together so they do not contradict each other.

BUY-4 and BUY-5 say 'Buy direct' and 'straight to the artist' over-promise. ARTIST-4 and BUY-6 want the buy button higher and more prominent. Making the button more prominent while it still leads to a message form increases the mismatch. Rename the label first (for example 'Ask to buy'), then raise it.

VISUAL-1 and DISCOVERY-3 want price and title always visible on desktop cards. This conflicts with the brutalist look of image-first cards and with the hover-driven reveal (VISUAL-8). Resolve it with a persistent small label strip and keep the hover for detail.

VISUAL-5 wants the loader and page curtain shortened or removed. These are part of the stepped 'cut-and-paste' brand motion and are used to hide image loading. Removing them without a fallback may expose layout shift. Shorten them, skip them on repeat visits and on lite devices.

RESPONSIVE-6 (two overlapping navigations) is fixed by dropping one of them, but IA-4 and DISCOVERY-8 depend on the bottom bar as the single consistent wayfinding. Keep the bottom bar and trim the hamburger.

BUY-8 and RESPONSIVE-2 want fewer fixed layers on the buy page, while BUY-1 and BUY-2 need a visible persistent status area for send results. Any new sticky feedback strip adds to the fixed-layer stack. Put feedback inline next to the send button and remove a sticky layer instead.

DISCOVERY-2 (sort should cover all works) and IA-3 (the wall shows only 8 of 30) interact. Making sort apply to all works means the wall must show all or paginate, which conflicts with the curated 8 picks that ARTIST-5 and DISCOVERY-7 also rely on. Decide whether the wall is curated or complete, and label it clearly.

drop_off_points.step: Landing: loader (1.7s) plus page curtain, a first viewport with no artwork or price, and a CTA under the fold or the phone bar
Finding the works: desktop nav has no link to the wall, which is 6-8 screens down behind brand-story sections, and the city map does not lead from a discipline to its works
Scanning and filtering the wall: price and title hidden until hover, a scrambled sort, only 8 of 30 works, and filter state lost on return
Studio hall and quick view: the hall starts below the first screen, the picture is a sliver, price and Buy are below the fold, and the first work may be sold
Trust check before contacting: fake contact address, template legal pages, no stated operator, prototype status unclear, no buyer protection
Buy page decision: blank shipping, baht, payment and returns information; 'Buy direct' leading to a message form
Sending the message: sticky bar covers the field, a failed send looks like success, captcha failure wipes input
Artist path: Join button skips the pitch, no timeline, contradictory 'no jury' and cost promises
